knowledge_point.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $I=\int 6 x\operatorname{cos}(2 x)\,\text{d}x$. Use integration by parts.

$$
\int uv^{\prime}\,\mathrm{d}x=uv-\int vu^{\prime}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Choose the linear factor as $u$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =6 x \\ u^{\prime} & =6 \\ v^{\prime} & =\operatorname{cos}(2 x) \\ v & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}uv & =6 x\left(\frac{\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}\right) \\ \int vu^{\prime}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(\frac{\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}\right)6\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the remaining integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{6 x\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}-3\int \operatorname{sin}(2 x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6 x\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}-3\left(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}(2 x)}{2}\right)+C \\  & =\frac{6 x\operatorname{sin}(2 x)}{2}+\frac{3\operatorname{cos}(2 x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $I=\int 2 x\operatorname{csc}^{2}(x - 3)\,\text{d}x$. Use integration by parts.

$$
\int uv^{\prime}\,\mathrm{d}x=uv-\int vu^{\prime}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

Choose the linear factor as $u$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =2 x \\ u^{\prime} & =2 \\ v^{\prime} & =\operatorname{csc}^{2}(x - 3) \\ v & =-\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}uv & =2 x\left(-\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)\right) \\ \int vu^{\prime}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(-\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)\right)2\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Use $t=\operatorname{sin}(x - 3)$ and $\mathrm{d}t=\operatorname{cos}(x - 3)\,\mathrm{d}x$. Evaluate the remaining integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-2 x\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)+2\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}(x - 3)}{\operatorname{sin}(x - 3)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2 x\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)+2\int \frac{1}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2 x\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)+2\ln|t|+C \\  & =-2 x\operatorname{cot}(x - 3)+2\ln|\operatorname{sin}(x - 3)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

This holds on each interval where $\operatorname{sin}(x - 3)\ne0$.

generation.domains: real x; sin(x+h) nonzero on each connected interval
